title: Cambridge IELTS 18 - Listening Test 1
summary: Bộ đề thi thử IELTS Listening chuẩn khảo thí trích từ Cambridge IELTS 18 Test 1

sections.title: Section 1: Moving Company & Transport Inquiry
sections.transcript:
[00:00] MAN: Excuse me. Would you mind if I asked you some questions? We're doing a survey on transport.
[00:08] SADIE: Yes, that's OK.
[00:11] MAN: First of all, can I take your name?
[00:14] SADIE: Yes. It's Sadie Jones.
[00:18] MAN: Thanks very much. And could I have your date of birth – just the year will do, actually. Is that all right?
[00:26] SADIE: Yes, that's fine. It's 1991.
[00:31] MAN: So next your postcode, please.
[00:34] SADIE: It's DW3Q 7YZ. [Q1]
[00:39] MAN: Great. Thanks. Is that in Wells?
[00:43] SADIE: No, it's actually in Harborne – Wells isn't far from there, though.
[00:50] MAN: I really like that area. My grandmother lived there when I was a kid.
[00:56] SADIE: Yes, it is nice.
[01:00] MAN: Right, so now I want to ask you some questions about how you travelled here today. Did you use public transport?
[01:09] SADIE: Yes. I came by bus.
[01:13] MAN: OK. And that was today. It's the 24th of April, isn't it? [Q2]
[01:20] SADIE: Isn't it the 25th? No, actually, you're right.
[01:26] MAN: Ha ha. And what was the reason for your trip today? I can see you've got some shopping with you.
[01:34] SADIE: Yes. I did some shopping but the main reason I came here was to go to the dentist. [Q3]
[01:43] MAN: That's not much fun. Hope it was nothing serious.
[01:48] SADIE: No, it was just a check-up. It's fine.
[01:52] MAN: Good. Do you normally travel by bus into the city centre?
[01:58] SADIE: Yes. I stopped driving in ages ago because parking was so difficult to find and it costs so much. [Q4]
[02:08] MAN: I see.
[02:10] SADIE: The bus is much more convenient too. It only takes about 30 minutes.
[02:17] MAN: That's good. So where did you start your journey?
[02:22] SADIE: At the bus stop on Claxby Street. [Q5]
[02:27] MAN: Is that C-L-A-X-B-Y?
[02:30] SADIE: That's right.
[02:35] MAN: And how satisfied with the service are you? Do you have any complaints?
[02:42] SADIE: Well, as I said, it's very convenient and quick when it's on time, but this morning it was late. Only about 10 minutes, but still. [Q6]
[02:55] MAN: Yes, I understand that's annoying. And what about the timetable? Do you have any comments about that?
[03:03] SADIE: Mmm. I suppose I mainly use the bus during the day, but any time I've been in town in the evening – for dinner or at the cinema – I've noticed you have to wait a long time for a bus – there aren't that many. [Q7]
[03:23] MAN: OK, thanks. So now I'd like to ask you about your car use.
[03:29] SADIE: Well, I have got a car but I don't use it that often. Mainly just to go to the supermarket. But that's about it really. My husband uses it at the weekends to go to the golf club. [Q8]
[03:48] MAN: And what about a bicycle?
[03:51] SADIE: I don't actually have one at the moment.
[03:55] MAN: What about the city bikes you can rent? Do you ever use those?
[04:01] SADIE: No – I'm not keen on cycling there because of all the pollution. But I would like to get a bike – it would be good to use it to get to work. [Q9]
[04:17] MAN: So why haven't you got one now?
[04:20] SADIE: Well, I live in a flat – on the second floor and it doesn't have any storage – so we'd have to leave it in the hall outside the flat. [Q10]
[04:34] MAN: I see. OK. Well, I think that's all …

sections.title: Section 2: Tour of the Sports Gym & Community Center
sections.transcript:
[00:02] Guide: Welcome to the tour of our newly revamped community sports gym, nothing but fitness.
[00:08] No doubt you know a little of what our gym has to give in terms of fitness, but as you'll discover, we have much more than just running machines and weights on offer.
[00:18] The gym's open from 05:30 AM, nice and early in the morning, to 10 PM at night, so these hours give you plenty of time to fit in your workouts in our weights and cardio rooms or with your personal trainers.
[00:32] Now onto children's services: we have a childcare centre on-site for moms and dads wanting to fit a workout into your busy day, but it's only open in the mornings, so you'll need to plan your workout around that.
[00:46] For those of you too busy to eat properly at home, there's a cafe on-site offering healthy and delicious meals that starts serving as soon as the gym opens and doesn't shut until we close at night.
[01:01] Of course, to work out comfortably, you need suitable clothing. We have a sports shop here for those of you who'd like to pick up some new shoes or workout gear. The staff there will be happy to kit you out from midday onwards, so do have a look at what's on offer.
[01:17] We're a modern gym, and we're always updating our facilities. Actually, the gym's just replaced all our treadmills with the latest models, so if you're a runner, try them out.
[01:29] Furthermore, we have thoroughly renovated and modernized the change rooms with luxury heated showers and digital lockers.
[01:39] Now, let me orient you using the floor map: directly across from reception is our yoga studio at point A, and right beside it at point B is our brand new Finnish sauna. The locker rooms are located along the eastern wing at point E...

sections.title: Section 3: Students Discussion on Renewable Energy Project
sections.transcript:
[00:05] Jack: Hi Emma, thanks for meeting up to discuss our environmental engineering assignment on offshore wind energy.
[00:12] Emma: Hi Jack! I've been reviewing our research questions. Why did we decide to focus specifically on offshore wind farms rather than onshore turbines?
[00:22] Jack: Well, the main reason was that coastal winds are considerably stronger and much more consistent throughout the year, yielding up to 40% more electricity.
[00:34] Emma: That's right. However, when examining policy constraints, the primary regulatory obstacle proved to be maritime zoning laws and environmental protection agreements for migratory sea birds.
[00:48] Jack: Exactly. What truly surprised me in the technical literature was the sheer mechanical efficiency of the latest 15-megawatt turbine generators.
[01:00] Emma: Our tutor, Dr. Harrison, suggested that we must include a life-cycle carbon assessment covering raw material extraction and offshore foundation installation.
[01:14] Jack: Agreed. For our project submission, who is doing what? Emma, would you be able to produce the technical diagrams and architectural schematics?
[01:24] Emma: Sure, I can draw the diagrams. And I can also conduct the field interviews with local harbor engineers.
[01:32] Jack: Great! I will handle the quantitative statistical analysis on wind velocity datasets.
[01:40] Emma: And for the literature review and final concluding section, let's both collaborate on writing those together.

sections.title: Section 4: University Lecture on Marine Biology & Cetaceans
sections.transcript:
[00:05] Professor: Good morning everyone. In today's marine biology lecture, we will explore the evolutionary adaptations and ecological challenges faced by cetaceans, including whales and dolphins.
[00:19] Cetaceans navigate and hunt in dark underwater environments primarily through echolocation, emitting high-frequency clicks and interpreting the returning sound echoes.
[00:32] Deep-diving species like sperm whales can descend to extraordinary ocean depths exceeding 2,000 meters in search of giant squid.
[00:44] In these abyssal zones, avoiding apex predators such as killer whales becomes critical for juvenile calves.
[00:54] Annual seasonal migration across thousands of kilometers allows baleen whales to feed in cold polar waters during summer and breed in warm equatorial lagoons.
[01:10] Ocean temperature variations directly influence the abundance of krill, their primary prey species.
[01:21] Complex social communication relies on intricate melodic whale songs that can propagate hundreds of miles across ocean basins.
[01:34] Unfortunately, anthropogenic plastic pollution presents a lethal hazard through ingestion and digestive blockages.
[01:46] Moreover, commercial shipping noise interferes with their delicate sensory navigation, leading to catastrophic disorientation and strandings.
[02:00] Effective global conservation agreements are urgent to preserve these majestic marine mammals for future generations.
